easyorders.name: EasyOrders
easyorders.intro: EasyOrders and Tallaby both charge per order instead of a monthly fee, and both are built for cash on delivery in Egypt. Here is how they differ on fees, payments, shipping and tools, with a source for every EasyOrders fact.
easyorders.priceNote: EasyOrders charges {eoOrderFee} per order on its Regular plan, or {eoPro} a month on Professional with no order fee, after a {eoActivation} wallet top-up to activate. It prices in US dollars, converted here at today's rate. Its pages don't say whether cancelled or fake orders are charged.
easyorders.cost: EasyOrders: {eoAtVolume} in order fees on Regular, or {eoPro} on Professional with no order fee.
verdictTallaby: You want a lower fee per order: Tallaby's Free plan is {orderFee} per order.
You want your store in Arabic and English, and a list of abandoned checkouts to follow up on WhatsApp.
You want your own Paymob or Kashier account and Bosta waybills in one dashboard.
verdict: You run ads to landing pages and funnels: EasyOrders has them ready, with an AI landing page from one line.
You need many shipping companies or sell outside Egypt: it advertises more than 100 carriers and sites for 10 countries.
Your store runs well there and you don't need anything it lacks. Moving takes time, so don't move without a clear reason.

shopify.name: Shopify
shopify.intro: Shopify is the biggest global store platform, and it works in Egypt with an Arabic dashboard. But Shopify Payments isn't offered in Egypt, so every card order carries an extra fee. Here is how it compares with Tallaby, with a source for every Shopify fact.
shopify.priceNote: Shopify's Basic plan is {shopifyBasic} a month on monthly billing (Grow {shopifyGrow}, Advanced {shopifyAdvanced}), priced in US dollars and converted here at today's rate. Because Shopify Payments isn't available in Egypt, Basic adds {shopifyGatewayFee} to every order paid through another provider such as Paymob or Kashier. Paid apps can come on top.
shopify.cost: Shopify: {shopifyBasic} on Basic, plus {shopifyGatewayFee} of every card or wallet order paid through Paymob, Kashier or another provider, on top of that provider's own fees. Cash-on-delivery orders pay no extra fee.
verdictTallaby: You sell in Egypt and want Paymob or Kashier with no extra platform fee on card orders.
You want cash on delivery, fake-order protection and Bosta built in, without paid apps.
You want to start with no monthly fee: Tallaby's Free plan is {orderFee} per order.
verdict: You sell in many countries and languages and need the largest app store.
You want AI to generate a store design from a description of your business.
Your store runs well there and you don't need anything it lacks. Moving takes time, so don't move without a clear reason.

strengths.title: The biggest ecosystem
strengths.body: More than 21,000 apps and over 1,300 themes, with official Google and Meta catalog apps.

strengths.title: Tools on every plan
strengths.body: Abandoned-checkout emails, email campaigns, chat support at any hour and the Sidekick AI assistant.

strengths.title: Room to grow abroad
strengths.body: Up to 20 storefront languages and plans that scale to very large stores.

expandcart.name: ExpandCart
expandcart.intro: ExpandCart sells monthly plans priced in Egyptian pounds and unlocks features by plan. Tallaby starts with no monthly fee, with the same tools on both plans. Here is how they compare, with a source for every ExpandCart fact.
expandcart.priceNote: ExpandCart's plans run from {ecStandard} a month (Standard: up to 100 products and 1 template) to {ecUltimate} a month (Ultimate), as listed on its pricing page, with a yearly discount and no sales commission.
expandcart.cost: ExpandCart: {ecStandard} a month on Standard, with no fee per order and no sales commission. A bigger catalog needs a higher plan.
verdictTallaby: You want to start with no monthly fee: Tallaby's Free plan is {orderFee} per order.
You want abandoned checkouts, email campaigns and every template on the plan you start with.
You want cash on delivery, fake-order protection and AI product writing from day one.
verdict: You want a fixed monthly price in Egyptian pounds and no fee per order.
You need an app marketplace or mature extras such as point of sale and loyalty.
Your store runs well there and you don't need anything it lacks. Moving takes time, so don't move without a clear reason.

salla.name: Salla
salla.intro: Salla is a leading Saudi store platform with a real free plan. When we checked, it served Saudi Arabia and the UAE, and opening a store needed Saudi documents. Here is how it compares with Tallaby for a seller in Egypt, with a source for every Salla fact.
salla.priceNote: Salla's Basic plan is free; Plus is {sallaPlus} a month and Pro {sallaPro} a month, priced in Saudi riyals and converted here at today's rate. A Salla store needs a Saudi commercial registration or freelance document, a Saudi mobile number and a Saudi bank account.
salla.cost: Salla: nothing on Basic, with no fee per order, but Basic takes only bank transfer and cash on delivery; card payments start on Plus at {sallaPlus} a month, plus the payment fees. A store needs Saudi papers, so it can't open from Egypt.
verdictTallaby: You sell from Egypt: Tallaby works with Egyptian documents, Paymob, Kashier and Bosta.
You want cash on delivery with fake-order protection and Egyptian shipping zones.
You want to start with no monthly fee: Tallaby's Free plan is {orderFee} per order.
verdict: You sell in Saudi Arabia or the UAE and can register a Saudi business.
You need Gulf payment methods such as mada, Apple Pay, Tabby and Tamara.
You want a very large app store and mature marketing tools for the Gulf.

zid.name: Zid
zid.intro: Zid is a Saudi store platform with an Egyptian site, prices in Egyptian pounds and a free Starter plan. Its Egyptian payment and shipping partners appear as logos on that site. Here is how it compares with Tallaby, with a source for every Zid fact.
zid.priceNote: Zid's Starter plan is free. In Egypt, Rise is {zidRise} a month and Growth {zidGrowth} a month on monthly billing, as listed on zid.eg, with a discount for yearly billing. Online card payments start on Rise.
zid.cost: Zid: nothing on Starter, with no fee per order, but Starter takes only bank transfer and cash on delivery; card payments start on Rise at {zidRise} a month, plus the payment fees.
verdictTallaby: You want card payments from the start: on Tallaby you connect your own Paymob or Kashier account on either plan.
You want fake-order protection, Bosta waybills and email campaigns without a paid plan.
You want to start with no monthly fee: Tallaby's Free plan is {orderFee} per order.
verdict: You want a free plan with no fee per order and can live without online payments at first.
You sell in Egypt and the Gulf and want one platform for both.
You need a big app store, point of sale or Amazon and Trendyol sales channels.
